free_tier.stated: 3 GB per free personal account. Anaconda staff on the official forum: 'You'll hit a hard limit at 10 GB with the default storage settings. If you need a large amount of storage (>100GB), you'll need to contact sales.' Team plan is 50 GB.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered for public packages. CDN-fronted (Cloudflare). conda-forge serves multi-GB packages anonymously with no auth.

record.tooling: anaconda-client (`anaconda upload`, `anaconda copy`, `anaconda remove`); REST at api.anaconda.org; conda itself is the client for download. Public channel listing is anonymous JSON.
record.chaining: Multiply by free orgs/accounts: 3 GB personal, 10 GB default cap, 50 GB Team. Even chained aggressively this is the smallest unit in the field. 10 TiB would need ~340 personal accounts at 3 GB. Not worth the operational cost against npm's 200 MB x unlimited.
record.limits_note: 3 GB personal free / 10 GB default hard limit / 50 GB Team. Per-package size not separately capped. Free accounts are public-only. Package versions can be removed but not edited.
record.reliability_note: Hard-limit enforcement is a real upload block, not a warning, and Anaconda's own forum answer routes anyone above 10 GB to sales. Storage ceiling is the smallest of the registries and there is no anonymous-way around it.

evidence.proved: 'the personal storage limit is only 3GB'; staff reply: 'You'll hit a hard limit at 10 GB with the default storage settings. If you need a large amount of storage (>100GB), you'll need to contact sales'
'The free plan allows you to search for, create and host public packages, and provides up to 3 GB storage space'
probe: GET -> 200, 3,868 files, 25.6 GB total for one package name (shows the platform itself carries far more than the free-tier limit — the limit is per publisher account, not per package)
